title: About Proximux
content: Proximux is a software engineering studio that ships production AI systems and software. We are a small, senior team and take on few projects so each one gets real senior attention. We build across four disciplines: enterprise RAG and knowledge engines, autonomous AI voice agents, cross-platform mobile apps, and custom full-stack web. Ask Proximux, the assistant on this site, runs on the same Retrieval-Augmented Generation approach we build for clients, so it is a live demo of the product. Get in touch at info@proximux.dev or book a discovery call.

title: Service: Enterprise RAG & Knowledge Engines
content: We build retrieval systems that answer from your data with citations, not hallucinations. Hybrid retrieval combines semantic search, keyword search, and reranking over your documents, wikis, and databases. Every answer is grounded in retrieved source chunks with inline citations so your team can verify each response, and low-confidence queries abstain instead of guessing. Deliverables include an ingestion pipeline (PDF, DOCX, HTML, Notion, Confluence, SQL), a chunking and embedding strategy tuned to your corpus, hybrid vector search with cross-encoder reranking, an inline citation layer, an evaluation harness on your own test set, and an admin dashboard with ingestion monitoring. Typical stack: Python, FastAPI, Pinecone or pgvector, OpenAI or Claude, LangGraph, Redis.

title: Service: Autonomous AI Voice Agents & Receptionists
content: We build end-to-end inbound and outbound voice agents with natural turn-taking and sub-second response. They answer FAQs from your knowledge base, qualify callers, book appointments, write to your CRM live, and hand off to a human with full call context. This is real conversation with barge-in and interruption handling, not a phone menu or IVR. Deliverables include telephony integration (Twilio, Vonage, SIP), a streaming speech-to-text to LLM to text-to-speech pipeline, function-calling for bookings, lookups, and CRM writes, live CRM and calendar sync, and call transcripts, summaries, and analytics. Typical stack: Python, FastAPI, Twilio, Deepgram, ElevenLabs or OpenAI Realtime, WebSockets.

title: Service: Cross-Platform Mobile Apps
content: We build production mobile apps in React Native and Expo: one codebase shipped to both the App Store and Play Store, with native performance. Apps are offline-first, push-enabled, and wired to a typed API, and we own the full lifecycle from architecture to build pipeline (EAS) to store submission and review handling. Deliverables include an iOS and Android app from one codebase, a typed API client with end-to-end types shared with the backend, an offline cache with background sync, push notifications, auth, and in-app payments, CI/CD via EAS with over-the-air updates, and store submission. Typical stack: React Native, Expo, TypeScript, FastAPI, Postgres, EAS.

title: Service: Custom Full-Stack Web Engineering
content: We build typed, tested, observable web applications from database schema to production deploy, on a Python and FastAPI backend with a modern React or Next.js front end. Everything is typed end to end, tested on critical paths, and deployed to infrastructure you own from day one. Deliverables include a FastAPI backend with a Postgres schema and migrations, REST and WebSocket APIs, background jobs and queues, a React or Next.js front end, auth with RBAC and audit logging, observability (logs, metrics, tracing) with CI/CD and infrastructure as code, and a full repo and infrastructure handover. Typical stack: Python, FastAPI, Postgres, React, TypeScript, Docker.

title: How we work: our process
content: Our process has three steps. First, a Discovery Call: we map the problem, constraints, and success metrics, then send a fixed-scope proposal with a timeline and price, no open-ended hourly billing. Second, Blueprint and Sandbox Demo: before the full build we ship a working sandbox, a real running slice of the system, so you validate on something real instead of slides, and you get an architecture diagram plus an interactive sandbox. Third, Production and Handover: we build, test, and deploy to infrastructure you own, and you get the repo, docs, and a walkthrough, with an optional retainer for iteration.

title: How we price
content: Pricing is fixed-scope and milestone-based, not open-ended hourly billing. You approve scope and price up front, and change requests are quoted separately so the number never drifts. We give a fixed timeline and price in the proposal after a discovery call, tailored to your project. For a precise quote and timeline, book a discovery call, where a founder gives a fixed-scope proposal.

title: Code ownership and IP
content: You own the code and IP, 100%. On final payment, all source code, IP, and infrastructure transfer to you. We keep nothing and lock you into nothing, and we can sign your NDA before the discovery call. After launch there is an optional retainer for iteration, monitoring, and support, with no lock-in: the repo and docs are yours to hand to any team.

title: What happens to your data
content: Your data stays in your own infrastructure and accounts wherever possible. We can run fully in your cloud using your own OpenAI, Pinecone, or AWS keys. Nothing you share is used to train any model.

title: Live demos
content: Two demos are live right now. Ask Proximux is this chat assistant: it answers questions about Proximux using full-text retrieval over our own content, the same RAG approach we build for clients. The second is a sentiment model we fine-tuned ourselves: a BERT model fine-tuned with LoRA (parameter-efficient fine-tuning) on real review data, served over FastAPI with a live confidence score, supporting single review, batch, and CSV upload. The voice agent and mobile app demos are coming soon and are not live yet.

title: Are we a fit, and how to verify we can build it
content: To see that we can build what you need, run the live demos on the Work page and look at our real project portfolio. Before any full engagement we ship a working sandbox so you validate on real output, not a pitch. If we are not a good fit, we will say so on the first call and point you to someone better. We take on few projects so the ones we take get real senior attention.
